title: A Saturday out in London
intro: Two plans for the same Saturday afternoon, made in different ways. Which would you rather do?

plans.title: Plan 1
summary: Start: Charing Cross station at 12:00 · 4 stops, including lunch
Costs: about £15 for food and entry, plus about £6 transport

stops.title: Lunch near Waterloo station
stops.travel_text: Getting there: about 12 min on foot from Charing Cross station.
stops.what: Pick a café, pub or food stall nearby.
lines: Getting there: about 12 min on foot from Charing Cross station.
Pick a café, pub or food stall nearby.
Food: about £15

stops.title: The Garden at 120: a rooftop garden among the City towers
stops.travel_text: Getting there: about 26 min: walk to Waterloo station, then take the Tube or bus to Bank, Monument or Fenchurch Street station.
stops.approach: Go into Hogarth Court from Fenchurch Street or Fenchurch Avenue, pass an airport-style security check, and take the lift to floor 15.
stops.what: You step out 15 floors up into a garden of wisteria, roses and hydrangeas around a water feature, with the City's towers all around and views to the Thames and Tower Bridge.

Cost: free

stops.title: St Dunstan-in-the-East: a ruined church garden hidden in the City
stops.travel_text: Getting there: about 6 min on foot from The Garden at 120.
stops.approach: Walk down St Dunstan's Hill towards the river.
stops.what: Among office blocks, you walk into the ruins of a medieval church that is now a public garden.
lines: Getting there: about 6 min on foot from The Garden at 120.
Walk down St Dunstan's Hill towards the river.

Cost: free

stops.title: Through Somerset House to the river terrace
stops.travel_text: Getting there: about 26 min: walk to Monument or Tower Hill station, then take the Tube or bus to the Strand entrance (Temple or Covent Garden station).
stops.approach: From the Strand, go through the arch into the courtyard, cross it, and go through to the River Terrace.
stops.what: From the busy Strand you pass through the arch into the big, quiet courtyard, then out onto the terrace, where the Thames opens up in front of you.
stops.rain_swap: A rest in the Royal Festival Hall's free foyers by the river, about 15 min away on foot.

plans.title: Plan 2
summary: Start: Charing Cross station at 12:00 · 4 stops, including lunch
Costs: about £15 for food and entry, plus about £3 transport

stops.title: The National Gallery
stops.travel_text: Getting there: about 5 min on foot from Charing Cross station.
stops.approach: Walk to Trafalgar Square and go in through the Sainsbury Wing entrance.
stops.what: Wander the free collection of paintings at your own pace.
lines: Getting there: about 5 min on foot from Charing Cross station.
Walk to Trafalgar Square and go in through the Sainsbury Wing entrance.
Wander the free collection of paintings at your own pace.
Cost: free

stops.title: Lunch at Borough Market
stops.travel_text: Getting there: about 20 min by Tube or bus from the National Gallery.
stops.approach: Walk to Westminster station and take the Jubilee line to London Bridge; the market is right beside the station.
stops.what: Graze the food stalls: pick a few things and eat as you wander.

Allow about 10 min to queue.

stops.title: Tate Modern: the Turbine Hall and the view from Level 10
stops.travel_text: Getting there: about 15 min on foot from Borough Market.
stops.approach: Walk west along Bankside, past Shakespeare's Globe.
stops.what: Walk into the vast Turbine Hall, look round the free collection, then take the lift from Level 1 up to Level 10 for a view over the Thames to St Paul's.

stops.title: Along the South Bank, past the London Eye
stops.travel_text: Getting there: about 3 min on foot from Tate Modern.
stops.approach: Start on the river path outside Tate Modern.
stops.what: Walk west past the Oxo Tower, the National Theatre and the Southbank Centre to the London Eye, with the river beside you. You walk past the London Eye; a ride isn't part of this plan.
stops.rain_swap: The Royal Festival Hall's free foyers, on the way (closed on Mondays).
